items.title: NDLEA 184.5kg cocaine bust: Court remands KC Luxury, two others
items.description: … Slams 22-count charge By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) on Friday arraigned Lagos-based luxury goods dealer Afolabi Kazeem Michael, popularly known as KayCee Luxury, and two others before the Federal High Court, Lagos, over the alleged export of 184.5 kilogrammes of cocaine to the United Kingdom. Afolabi was arraigned alongside Boniface Freeman Ochoche Sule and Ikechukwu Ekugo Patriarch before Justice Ayokunle Olayinka Faji on a 22-count charge bordering on alleged cocaine trafficking, illegal export of narcotics and money laundering. Prosecution counsel, Abu Ibrahim, told the court that the defendants allegedly conspired between July 28 and August 1, 2026, with Atandare Oladipupo Oluwarotimi and Latifat Yusuf, who have reportedly been arrested in London in connection with the case, to export the illicit drug concealed in five consignments through a Lagos-based courier logistics firm. According to the prosecution, the consignments, bearing Airway Bill Numbers 2079998314, 8224082370, 2079973571, 7181131742 and 2211893902, were shipped under the name “Yemi Ejide” before being intercepted by NDLEA operatives. The charge, marked FHC/LAG/CR/755/2026, alleged that Afolabi procured a staff member of BOT Express Logistics on Lagos Island to process the consignments and paid N13.2 million from a Mallamawa Ventures Zenith Bank account to the logistics firm for the shipment. The prosecution further alleged that Boniface procured Ikechukwu to facilitate the export, while Afolabi was accused of unlawfully possessing the 184.5kg of cocaine intended for export. The NDLEA also filed 16 counts of alleged money laundering against Afolabi under the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022. The agency alleged that he channelled several billions of naira through a network of companies and personal accounts, including Mallamawa Ventures, Fateey Man Multi-Purpose Nigeria Limited, Patonifa Limited, Ade-Lak Resources, Holmestas Global Services Limited and La Capital Enterprises. According to the prosecution, the funds were allegedly used to acquire motor vehicles and landed properties in an attempt to conceal proceeds allegedly linked to illicit activities. He was also accused of failing to declare his assets. The three defendants pleaded not guilty to all 22 counts. The prosecution opposed their bail applications and urged the court to remand them in custody pending trial, citing the gravity of the alleged offences. Justice Faji consequently ordered that the defendants be remanded in NDLEA custody and adjourned the matter until October 4, 2026, for ruling on their bail applications. The NDLEA had earlier said Afolabi, who allegedly presented himself online as a luxury goods dealer and lifestyle influencer under names including KayCee Luxury, KayCee Lux, KC, Mr. Luxury and Yemi Ejide, was arrested on August 13, 2026, while allegedly attempting to leave Nigeria on a business-class flight to Paris from the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos. The agency said his arrest followed the interception of the cocaine consignment, which it valued at about N39 billion. According to the NDLEA, a search of his person and apartment in Banana Island, Lagos, led to the recovery of exotic vehicles, foreign currencies and jewellery, which the agency said were suspected proceeds of illicit trade. items.title: Washington refuse qu’Anthropic et OpenAI soumettent leurs derniers modèles à une évaluation indépendante
items.description: La Maison-Blanche a demandé à certains laboratoires américains d’IA, dont OpenAI et Anthropic, de réserver l’accès à leurs nouveaux modèles de frontière aux tests du gouvernement américain avant de les partager avec d’autres organismes d’évaluation indépendants, comme l’AI Security Institute (UK AISI), qui fait référence dans le domaine White House asks OpenAI and Anthropic to hold new models from UK testers until US review », Politico , 24 septembre 2026.'> 4 . L’administration américaine remettrait ainsi en cause l’accès privilégié pré-déploiement dont disposait jusqu’ici cet institut public britannique. L’ordre d’accès aux nouveaux modèles de frontière serait désormais le suivant : d’abord, une évaluation par le gouvernement américain, puis la sécurisation des systèmes américains, et seulement ensuite le partage du modèle avec des partenaires étrangers. L'institut UK AISI est l’un des principaux organismes publics au monde spécialisés dans l’évaluation pré et post-déploiement des modèles de frontière. Créé en novembre 2023 à la suite du sommet sur la sécurité de l’IA de Bletchley Park, il évalue la plupart des modèles à la frontière et documente notamment leurs capacités cyber, biologiques et chimiques, l’autonomie des agents ou encore les risques liés à l’auto-amélioration récursive de l’IA. Comme d’autres organisations indépendantes d’évaluation (METR, Redwood Research notamment), le UK AISI pouvait bénéficier d’un accès anticipé à des checkpoints pré-déploiement grand public afin d’effectuer les tests sur ses propres benchmarks pour documenter la progression des capacités et des risques associés aux modèles d’IA. Début septembre, le Financial Times rapportait que le UK AISI n’avait pas eu accès à Mythos 5.1, alors qu’il disposait historiquement d’un accès anticipé aux principaux modèles américains Anthropic withheld latest AI model from UK testing agency », Financial Times , 9 septembre 2026.'> 5 . Auparavant, OpenAI, Anthropic et Google DeepMind ont tous fourni à l’Institut un accès à certains de leurs modèles les plus avancés afin qu’ils soient testés. Cette évolution intervient alors que les capacités cyber des modèles de frontière deviennent un sujet de sécurité nationale. En juin, l’administration américaine avait déjà imposé des contrôles à l’exportation sur Fable et Mythos, les modèles d’Anthropic, notamment en raison de l’amélioration rapide de leurs capacités dans le domaine de la cybersécurité, interdisant ainsi leur utilisation par des ressortissants étrangers. La NSA teste désormais les modèles avancés pour identifier des vulnérabilités susceptibles d’affecter les systèmes de renseignement et de défense et développe ses propres évaluations. L’agence y consacrerait plusieurs milliards de dollars par an, principalement en capacités de calcul Classified Estimates Show the NSA Is Paying Billions to Test AI Models », The Washington Sun , 24 septembre 2026.'> 6 . L’équivalent direct américain du UK AISI, le Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), reste beaucoup plus limité en moyens que l’institut britannique. Hébergé au NIST, le CAISI est sous-financé et dispose d’effectifs de recherche plus réduits. Les laboratoires d’IA ont également proposé une évaluation directement entre laboratoires, sans supervision gouvernementale. Ils testeraient ainsi réciproquement leurs modèles avant leur mise sur le marché. Google, OpenAI et Anthropic travaillent conjointement à la création d’un organisme privé de normalisation consacré à la sécurité de l’IA, qui pourrait définir des standards communs d’évaluation pré-déploiement. La question autour des capacités d’évaluation indépendantes devient d’autant plus centrale que les capacités et les architectures des modèles évoluent. Redwood Research souligne notamment que certaines architectures pourraient réduire fortement la capacité d’évaluateurs humains à surveiller et auditer le comportement des modèles, alors qu’ils raisonnent non plus via une chaîne de pensée textuelle compréhensible mais via des états latents internes non observables directement et. al. , Latent reasoning architectures would undermine CoT, our strongest oversight tool , Redwood Research, 23 septembre 2026.'> 7 . Au-delà des tests et rapports d’évaluation, cette asymétrie d’accès aux modèles frontières touche dans les usages l’industrie européenne. Le projet Glasswing, le programme d’Anthropic donnant un accès anticipé à Mythos, a permis dès avril aux banques et entreprises critiques américaines de renforcer leur défense cyber, notamment en recherchant avec Mythos des vulnérabilités dans leurs propres systèmes. Les banques européennes n’y ont eu accès que plusieurs mois plus tard. L’article Washington refuse qu’Anthropic et OpenAI soumettent leurs derniers modèles à une évaluation indépendante est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: US joins Elon Musk fight against €120m EU fine
items.description: By Juliet Umeh, Agency report The United States Government has joined billionaire Elon Musk’s legal battle against the European Union (EU) seeking to overturn a €120 million fine imposed on his social media platform, X, over alleged breaches of the bloc’s digital rules. The US Department of Justice, DOJ, has asked the General Court of the Court of Justice of the European Union for permission to intervene in support of X and Musk in their bid to annul the European Commission’s December 2025 decision. The move raises the stakes in an increasingly contentious debate between Washington and Brussels over the regulation of American technology companies operating in Europe. Assistant Attorney General for the DOJ’s Civil Division, Brett Shumate, accused the European Commission of regulatory overreach. “The European Commission inappropriately attempted to expand its regulatory authority to reach American companies not present or operating within its jurisdiction,” Shumate said. “We will not tolerate the European Commission engaging in regulatory overreach to try and control American engines of innovation and economic growth.” The European Commission fined X €120 million for alleged violations of transparency obligations under the Digital Services Act, DSA. The Commission cited what it described as the “deceptive design” of X’s blue checkmark system, inadequate transparency in its advertising repository and failure to provide researchers sufficient access to public data. It argued that allowing users to obtain verified status without meaningful identity verification could expose users to impersonation, scams and manipulation. However, the US government said the case could have wider consequences for American technology companies, particularly regarding how far European regulators can extend their authority. The DOJ also objected to what it described as the extension of regulatory scrutiny to Musk personally and other companies under his ownership despite their alleged lack of connection to the digital services involved. The legal battle could now become a significant test of the reach of Europe’s digital regulatory regime and its implications for US technology companies. items.description: Le Camarade Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a reçu en audience, ce vendredi 25 septembre 2026, une délégation de l’Association africaine des centrales d’achats de médicaments essentiels (ACAME), conduite par le président du Bureau de l’Assemblée générale, Dr Ibrahim Kouyaté. Les échanges ont porté sur la tenue de la 26ᵉ Assemblée générale ordinaire de l’Association et sur la contribution des centrales d’achat au renforcement de la souveraineté pharmaceutique en Afrique. ‎ ‎La délégation a présenté au Chef du Gouvernement les principales articulations de cette Assemblée générale, qui se tient les 25 et 26 septembre 2026, à Ouagadougou. ‎Cette rencontre donnera notamment le coup d’envoi des activités commémoratives du trentième anniversaire de l’ACAME. Elle sera également consacrée à l’examen et à la validation des états financiers de l’Association pour l’exercice 2025. ‎ ‎Au cours de l’audience, la délégation a salué l’engagement du Burkina Faso, qui abrite le siège de l’ACAME. Elle a également mis en avant l’expérience de la Centrale d’achat des médicaments essentiels génériques (CAMEG), présentée comme une référence pour les centrales membres. « Nous avons une association forte. Les membres sont engagés et les résultats sont bons, ce qui permet d’entrevoir un avenir meilleur pour l’ensemble de nos centrales d’achat, qui ont décidé de mutualiser leurs forces et leurs connaissances, afin que nous puissions avoir une force de négociation auprès des fournisseurs pharmaceutiques, pour une meilleure accessibilité aux produits de santé au profit de nos populations », a indiqué Dr Ibrahim Kouyaté, à l’issue de l’audience. ‎Le Premier ministre a félicité l’ACAME pour sa contribution à l’amélioration de l’accès aux médicaments. ‎Il a réaffirmé la disponibilité du Burkina Faso à accompagner l’Association, conformément à la volonté du Gouvernement de faire de l’accès à des soins et à des médicaments de qualité un pilier de la souveraineté sanitaire. Abordant les enjeux de souveraineté pharmaceutique, le Chef du Gouvernement a appelé les centrales d’achat à jouer un rôle moteur dans la promotion d’une industrie pharmaceutique locale. ‎ ‎Il a insisté sur la mutualisation des efforts pour renforcer les capacités de production du continent et répondre aux besoins des populations. ‎« La question du médicament est une question de souveraineté. Nous devons mutualiser nos efforts pour que l’Afrique produise ce qu’elle consomme et garantisse à ses populations des produits de santé accessibles », a souligné le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo. ‎ ‎Créée le 19 juillet 1996 à Ouagadougou, l’ACAME regroupe aujourd’hui 22 centrales nationales d’achat. Elle a pour mission d’améliorer les performances de ses membres, afin de garantir aux populations la disponibilité et l’accessibilité de médicaments essentiels de qualité. ‎ ‎𝐃𝐂𝐑𝐏/𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞

items.title: Botola Pro : la montée en première et deuxième divisions soumise au respect du cahier des charges
items.description: La performance sportive ne suffira plus à elle seule pour accéder aux championnats professionnels de première et deuxième divisions. La Ligue nationale de football professionnel (LNFP) rappelle que les clubs devront également satisfaire à l’ensemble des exigences réglementaires, administratives, techniques et infrastructurelles prévues par le cahier des charges. La course à la montée en Botola Pro « Inwi » ne se jouera donc pas uniquement sur les terrains. Dans un communiqué publié vendredi, la LNFP a précisé que l’accession aux championnats professionnels de 1ère et 2è Divisions reste conditionnée au respect de plusieurs critères fixés par les règlements en vigueur. Ainsi, un club qui obtient sportivement une place lui permettant de monter devra encore démontrer sa conformité avec les exigences du cahier des charges avant que son accession ne soit définitivement validée. Les conditions à remplir concernent plusieurs aspects du fonctionnement des clubs. Elles portent notamment sur les infrastructures et les installations sportives, mais également sur les volets organisationnels, techniques et administratifs. La LNFP rappelle que ces exigences constituent une condition nécessaire à l’intégration des clubs dans les compétitions professionnelles. L’objectif est notamment de s’assurer que les équipes promues disposent des moyens et des structures nécessaires pour évoluer dans le championnat concerné. Une commission chargée de valider les accessions La validation définitive de la montée ne sera pas automatique. Elle relèvera d'une commission spécialisée, chargée d’examiner la situation des clubs concernés et de vérifier leur conformité avec l’ensemble des critères prévus par le cahier des charges. Cette commission devra ainsi se prononcer sur l’homologation de l’accession après avoir étudié les différents éléments du dossier. La LNFP appelle les clubs à anticiper À travers cette mise au point, la Ligue invite les clubs engagés dans la course à la promotion à veiller dès maintenant au respect de toutes les conditions requises. Un club pourrait donc obtenir sportivement son accession sans pour autant voir celle-ci définitivement homologuée s’il ne répond pas aux exigences prévues par le cahier des charges. Pour la LNFP, ce dispositif vise à garantir le bon déroulement des compétitions, à prévenir les déséquilibres entre les clubs et à assurer l’égalité des chances entre les différentes formations. La Ligue entend ainsi faire du respect des normes réglementaires et des exigences professionnelles un élément indissociable de la promotion sportive, aussi bien en première qu’en deuxième division. items.title: FBR sets up faceless tax audit, assessment centre in Islamabad
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has established the National Faceless Centre in Islamabad, under which audits and assessments will be handled by “faceless” wings to reduce official discretion and direct contact between tax officials and taxpayers. The initiative has been taken under Pakistan’s New Tax Operating Model and was approved by the government in principle in June. The centralised and faceless tax model is similar to systems used in the UK, Australia, the Netherlands, Singapore and India. It is designed to eliminate physical contact between tax authorities and taxpayers to prevent corruption. The decision to establish the National Faceless Centre was taken the Board in Council — a body headed by the FBR chairperson — in its meeting on Friday, an FBR statement said. It described NFC as a major reform that “changes how tax audits and assessments are carried out in Pakistan”. Until now, a taxpayer whose return was picked for audit had to deal with a particular officer in a particular office, often in person. Under the new system, that contact ends. Cases will be selected by a computerised, risk-based system rather than by any officer. Each case will then be assigned automatically to an officer who may be sitting anywhere in the country. The taxpayer will not know who the officer is, and the officer will have no say in which case comes to them. Every case will pass through three separate hands. One officer will conduct the audit, a second will make the assessment, and a third will review the work for quality before any order is issued. No single officer will control a taxpayer’s case from start to finish. All notices, replies and hearings will take place electronically through FBR’s IRIS system, and where the law requires a physical verification or recovery, it will be carried out by a separate field team, the statement detailed. The NFC draws its legal authority from the Finance Act, 2026. It will be headed by an Inland Revenue chief commissioner, with dedicated wings for faceless audit, faceless assessment, quality control and field operations. A Programme Management Unit has already been set up to oversee its rollout. “The purpose of the reform is same rules for every taxpayer, decisions based on data rather than personal judgement, and an end to the face to face contact that has long been a source of complaints. FBR expects the NFC to make tax proceedings faster, fairer and more transparent for taxpayers across Pakistan,” the statement said.

items.title: Indian police use tear gas against protesters seeking election chief's ouster
items.description: Indian police used tear gas and water cannons on Friday to disperse opposition Congress party members during nationwide protests demanding the resignation of the head of the election commission, whom they accuse of manipulating voter rolls. The “cockroach” youth movement, which counts millions of supporters and forced the education minister out in July, said it would launch protests across India on Oct 2 if Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar does not resign by Saturday. The protests, which are backed by other opposition groups, mark a new political challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi as Kumar, 62, a former civil servant, was appointed to head the independent Election Commission of India by Modi’s government. “Theft of votes is happening across the country,” local Congress party leader Amarinder Singh Raja said in Chandigarh in the northwest, one of at least two places where police fired water cannon after protesters climbed buses and barricades. Congress and other opposition parties have accused the eleciton commission of colluding with Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to manipulate voter lists and win state elections in recent years, charges both the commission and the BJP have denied. Kumar himself has not commented. Newspaper reports dissent within the commission In at least a dozen of India’s 28 states, Congress supporters shouted slogans against Kumar, held up posters demanding his arrest and in one instance, burned an effigy of him and Modi. In the capital Delhi, hundreds of protesters climbed barricades and hurled insults at a man wearing a Kumar mask. The demonstrations were triggered by a report in the Indian Express newspaper on Wednesday that Kumar’s deputies had questioned him over changes to voter lists that opposition groups say benefit Modi’s BJP. “For three years, I have been exposing vote theft. Now, the election commissioners themselves are acknowledging it and bringing the truth to light,” Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said late on Thursday, referring to Kumar’s deputies. “Gyanesh Kumar has committed treason. He should resign immediately,” he added. The Election Commission said differences among officers were normal in any institution and that all its actions were lawful. The BJP dismissed the report and said that opposition parties were indulging in a smear campaign because popular support for the BJP meant they lost elections. State elections next year — including in the most populous state, Uttar Pradesh, and Modi’s home state of Gujarat, both ruled by the BJP — are key tests of support ahead of parliamentary elections due in 2029.

items.description: D'intenses combats ont opposé dans la nuit de jeudi 24 septembre, les forces fédérales éthiopiennes à des troupes des autorités rebelles du Tigré dans la ville d'Abala, dans l'État régional voisin de l'Afar. Les forces fédérales "ont empêché les rebelles d'entrer dans la ville" située au sein de massifs marquant la frontière avec l'est du Tigré.

items.title: Linguère : une femme retrouvée pendue à Thiel
items.description: Un drame s’est produit jeudi 24 septembre 2026 à Thiel, dans le département de Linguère. Une femme âgée de 36 ans, identifiée sous le prénom de Sadio Kâ, a été retrouvée pendue à un arbre. Alertés, les éléments de la brigade de gendarmerie de Thiel, accompagnés de l’infirmier-chef de poste et des sapeurs-pompiers, se sont rendus sur les lieux pour procéder au constat. Le corps sans vie a ensuite été acheminé au centre hospitalier Amadou Magatte Lô de Linguère. Une enquête a été ouverte par les services compétents afin de déterminer les circonstances exactes du décès. Abdoulaye SADIO (Correspondant)

items.title: Fonsis : le Fonds islamique de Relance injecte 600 millions FCFA dans quatre entreprises
items.description: Le Fonds islamique de Relance (FIR), filiale du Fonds souverain d’investissements stratégiques (Fonsis), poursuit son accompagnement des entreprises sénégalaises. Il a formalisé, mardi 22 septembre, un investissement global de 600 millions de FCFA au profit de quatre entreprises opérant dans l’agroalimentaire, l’agro-industrie et l’enseignement scientifique. Les bénéficiaires sont Agro Industries du Nord (AIN), Mintou Rassoul, Bassari Baobab et l’École scientifique internationale d’Excellence (ESIEX). Réparties entre Saint-Louis, Tambacounda, Dakar et Keur Massar, ces structures bénéficieront de financements en fonds propres destinés notamment à moderniser leurs outils de production, renforcer leurs capacités de stockage et d’approvisionnement et développer de nouvelles infrastructures éducatives. Renforcer la filière rizicole Dans la vallée du fleuve Sénégal, le FIR accompagne deux entreprises engagées dans la filière rizicole. Implantée à Ross-Béthio, Agro Industries du Nord transforme le riz paddy dans une unité disposant d’une capacité de décorticage de trois tonnes par heure. Son investissement sera consacré à l’installation d’équipements solaires et à l’augmentation de ses capacités de stockage, avec l’objectif de mieux sécuriser son approvisionnement. De son côté, Mintou Rassoul, basée dans la région de Saint-Louis, produit, transforme et commercialise du riz blanc et du riz étuvé ainsi que différents sous-produits de transformation. La modernisation de son unité doit permettre d’améliorer la qualité de ses produits et d’augmenter les volumes de production. À travers ces deux opérations, le FIR entend contribuer au développement de la production et de la transformation locales du riz, tout en soutenant l’emploi dans la vallée du fleuve Sénégal et en renforçant l’offre nationale face aux importations. Le pari sur les produits agroforestiers À Tambacounda, l’investissement concerne Bassari Baobab, une entreprise spécialisée dans la valorisation de produits agroforestiers locaux, notamment le baobab, le bissap et le gingembre. Commercialisés sous les marques Zahra et Mouna, ces produits bénéficieront d’un renforcement des capacités de l’entreprise à travers la modernisation de ses équipements et la mise à niveau de ses espaces de production et de stockage. L’entreprise compte actuellement 60 employés, dont une majorité de femmes. Pour le FIR, cette opération illustre également sa volonté d’élargir l’accès à ses solutions de financement aux petites et moyennes entreprises sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Un investissement dans la formation scientifique Le quatrième bénéficiaire est l’École scientifique internationale d’Excellence (ESIEX), créée en 2019 au sein du Groupe Supdeco. L’établissement, implanté à Dakar, assure une formation allant du secondaire aux classes préparatoires et prépare ses élèves aux concours des grandes écoles d’ingénieurs. Le financement du FIR doit permettre d’équiper son futur campus de Keur Massar, de développer ses laboratoires et d’acquérir du matériel destiné à l’enseignement scientifique. Pour Abdoul Aziz Sy, PDG du Groupe Supdeco, cet appui répond à un enjeu stratégique pour le Sénégal : renforcer la formation de scientifiques et préparer les compétences dont le pays aura besoin dans les prochaines années. 7,5 milliards FCFA d’investissements cumulés Avec cette nouvelle opération, le FIR franchit un nouveau palier. Selon Babacar Gning, directeur général du Fonsis, le montant cumulé des investissements réalisés par le fonds, sous forme de fonds propres et de prêts Moudharaba, atteint désormais 7,5 milliards de FCFA. Pour Adramé Ndione, directeur du FIR, l’objectif est de proposer des solutions de financement à des entreprises de secteurs et de profils différents, en les rendant accessibles aux PME partout au Sénégal, au plus près de leurs activités et de leurs besoins. Filiale du Fonsis issue d’un partenariat entre le Fonsis, la Banque islamique de développement et l’État du Sénégal, le Fonds islamique de Relance dispose d’une enveloppe de 20 milliards de FCFA. Il propose aux PME des solutions de financement fondées sur des instruments de finance islamique afin d’accompagner la relance et le développement de leurs activités.

items.title: Obi to editors: Hold politicians accountable, insist on issue-based campaigns
items.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerian editors to hold politicians accountable ahead of the 2027 general election, insisting that campaigns must focus on good governance, security, national unity and economic prosperity. Obi also called on the media to ensure that political parties and candidates are allowed to campaign freely across the country, warning that intimidation and restrictions on political activities could undermine democracy. He made the call on Friday while speaking on the second day of the 22nd All Nigeria Editors Conference (ANEC) in Enugu, where he urged journalists to question politicians about their records, qualifications, policies and campaign promises. The former Anambra governor said the media had a responsibility to guide political discourse and challenge candidates who resorted to name-calling and personal attacks rather than discussing issues affecting Nigerians. “And for me today, as we approach election, I have only one thing I will plead that you include in your discussion. We made a choice to be a democratic country, and that choice is a choice that can help our country to grow,” Obi said. “And it is important that you help us, the politicians, to ensure that as we approach election, number one, that our discussions, our campaigns, everything we do, is strictly based on issues that will bring good governance, that will bring unity, security, and prosperity for the country. Strictly.” He urged editors to challenge politicians who deviated from issue-based campaigns and ensure that the 2027 elections were free, fair and credible. “You can guide us. If anybody steps out of it and goes into name-calling, or anything, you say, ‘No, no, no, no! That’s not the issue. You shouldn’t go there.’ That you ensure that we have free, fair, and credible election. If anybody stops anybody from campaigning, you say, ‘No.'” Obi cited past political campaigns in Anambra State to illustrate how politicians from different parties could engage in electoral contests without hostility. He recalled that during his second tenure as governor, former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola visited Anambra to campaign for Chris Ngige, who was then in the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN). According to Obi, he provided Fashola with his official convoy and remained in his office because he did not have a second set of vehicles. “It was me who gave Fashola my convoy. And because I don’t have two convoys, I didn’t go out of my office that day. I gave him everything, and stayed back in my office.” He said Fashola had asked where they would meet, but he explained that he would remain in his office while the former Lagos governor used his convoy. “Fashola is still there. You can go and ask him,” Obi said. The NDC candidate also recalled that former President Olusegun Obasanjo campaigned for Andy Uba in Anambra while Obi was governor, adding that he accompanied the former president during the campaign. “Obasanjo came… Obasanjo came to campaign for Andy Uba, I followed him. Everybody who is in Anambra was there. Some of you are there. He raised Andy Uba’s hand and said, ‘He’s the one, he’s incoming, I’m the outgoing.’ No problem, and I’m contesting the same—we didn’t quarrel!” Obi further recalled that former Abia State Governor Orji Uzor Kalu campaigned for Uche Ekwunife, saying he welcomed the delegation and provided lunch. “Orji Uzor Kalu came for Uche Ekwunife, we did not quarrel, I gave them lunch! When they finished, he said, ‘Uche will take over from me,’ no quarrel. It is the people!” He said such examples demonstrated the need for a peaceful political environment where candidates could freely seek votes across state boundaries. Obi dismisses rift with Soludo The former Anambra governor also dismissed suggestions that he was engaged in a political feud with his successor, Chukwuma Soludo, saying the two maintained a cordial relationship. Obi said he respected Soludo as governor and had no personal disagreement with him, despite the controversy surrounding allegations that his administration left debts behind. “There’s no issue between me and Soludo. Me and Soludo are close. As a banker, he was my customer. And we have not changed. If I see him, I greet him, I respect his office—he’s the governor.” He said he wanted to campaign for voters in Enugu and other states, stressing that the governor of a state did not determine the choices of all its residents. “But I want to campaign for the people of Enugu. Is that the people of Enugu? He has one vote. The same thing is what we want, and you can help us to do that.” Obi also disclosed that he and his wife were godparents to Soludo’s children, insisting that political disagreements should not be interpreted as a personal quarrel. “Don’t allow us to do… now people see me and say… if you watch the same interview, they say, “Oh, what is between you and Soludo? Whether you’re owing or not owing.” I said, Soludo is my respected elder brother. Any day, anytime! People might not know, I and my wife are godparents to Soludo’s children. Yes, we’re that close!” He added, “So we’re not quarrelling! And we will never quarrel! If I see him any day, me and him will hug and everything.” I left Anambra with $150m, Obi insists Obi again maintained that he did not leave Anambra State in debt when he completed his tenure in 2014, insisting that he left $150 million in savings. The former governor made the remarks amid allegations by the Anambra government that his administration left outstanding financial obligations. He said the money he left in savings was sufficient to cover the liabilities being discussed, arguing that the state could have settled the alleged debt and retained substantial funds. “If they say anything, I’ll answer them. Like I said yesterday, I did not leave debt in Anambra State. If you like, go and see that interview. The day I left office, thank God, Oti confirmed it this morning while on Arise, I left $150 million in savings. No other governor has left dollars. If you see one, tell me. I left $150 million.” Obi said he was not raising the issue to boast or attack the current administration, adding that he had inherited a different financial position when he assumed office. “And that is it, I’m not quarrelling with them, I’m not saying this as a boast. The day I came in, I explained it to them, what I met was $18 million debt. When I left, it was $30 million. I left $150 million.” He argued that even if the state had incurred the $120 million debt being discussed, the savings he left could have generated enough returns to cover the amount. “So even if you say all the money they said Anambra is owing, $120 million, and it was created by me, which is wrong public accounting—I said it yesterday—the money I left was giving Anambra State $10 million every year. So if you have been paying it 10-10 million, you would have finished paying it now, and the capital will still be remaining.” Obi said the money would have grown significantly if it had remained untouched, adding that the state could have paid the alleged debt and retained a substantial balance. He used an inheritance analogy to explain his position, saying the administration that inherited the funds should have settled the outstanding obligations rather than accuse his government of leaving the state indebted. “So, it’s a case of a father who allowed his children to inherit N100 million, but they said he’s owing N10 million, and they’re saying he’s owing debt. When they should have just paid it, and take their change, and be celebrating the man for making them rich.” The former governor said he had no intention of insulting serving governors or officials of the Federal Government, insisting that disagreements over public policies should be addressed through constructive arguments. “I cannot abuse any governor. I cannot abuse anybody in government. I don’t need to abuse people even in federal government. I’ve never abused anybody. Who has seen me calling President Tinubu’s name? Never! I will not do that. He’s the President of the country, he has all my respect.” He, however, said public officials should be open to scrutiny and criticism over their performance. “But I can argue on other issues, whether you’re doing well, or you’re not doing the right thing. That is allowed. We must, because the leader… the character and behavior of the leader exemplifies the value of the society. And the leader must live it.” Obi urges editors to question candidates directly Obi called on editors to scrutinise politicians based on their backgrounds, qualifications, public statements and records in office, saying candidates must personally answer questions about allegations against them. He criticised the practice of politicians relying on aides and supporters to respond to allegations, insisting that voters deserved direct explanations from those seeking public office. “It’s time for you people to get involved. Question us based on our background. Question us based on what we say. Question us for our qualification and everything. It’s not enough for anybody to say, “I’m this and this.” No!” He said politicians should not avoid answering allegations by sending proxies to defend them. “Anything they say about you, you must come and explain, and don’t do it through any proxy. Come and explain, because we are not voting for your wife, we are not voting for your children, we are not voting for your uncle or people representing you. We are voting for you, and we want you to come and answer what we want. That’s how it works.” Obi also urged journalists to contact him directly if allegations emerged during the campaign, saying he would respond personally and apologise if the claims were true. “It’s a campaign. You’ll be hearing me in campaign. If there’s anything you want to… if they tell you anything about me, please, feel free, call me and say, “Peter, people say you were a thief, or you stole when you were in secondary school, or you did not do this.” I will explain it to you, and if it’s true, I will apologize, because I’m a Christian, we do go to confession and they forgive us our sins.” He said acknowledging wrongdoing was necessary for building a society where younger generations could learn from the mistakes of public figures. Obi added that Nigeria had no alternative as a country and warned that political instability would affect everyone. “That’s what makes a society. So, if any of us have done something wrong, come out and tell us. So that the children can learn, so they can be able to know this is wrong, he has admitted wrongdoing.” He added, “Don’t think that we know everything. Don’t think that we’re everything, no. Please, we have no other nation except this one.” “And anarchy consumes everybody. If anything goes wrong in this country, please, it will consume all of you.” Obi criticises spending on government hospitals The former Anambra governor also called on journalists to investigate government spending on healthcare, alleging that inadequate funding of public hospitals had contributed to the country’s poor healthcare delivery. He said many Nigerians in rural communities lacked access to hospitals and primary healthcare facilities, forcing some to rely on religious centres for medical assistance. Obi said the government needed to invest in hospitals rather than leave citizens dependent on faith-based interventions for illnesses. “I spent time, I listened to you now talk about health, fantastic. But Doctor, my brother, this thing you’re saying can only happen in Port Harcourt. If anybody is sick in my village, the only thing they go to is church to pray, you know, because they have no hospital, they have no primary healthcare.” He added that healthcare challenges had become so severe that many sick people turned to religious centres because they had nowhere else to seek treatment. “That’s why if you go to where they’re doing deliverance now, there’s more sick people than in hospital, because there’s no hospital for them to go.” Obi urged politicians to stop presenting healthcare development as an impossible task, saying journalists should question government spending priorities. “And it’s not a difficult thing. Let politicians tell you… don’t listen to us that it’s difficult, it’s not difficult. You people help to help us question it.” He cited the University College Hospital in Ibadan and the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital in Enugu, saying they had previously attracted patients from outside their immediate locations but had since experienced a decline in their standing. “Ibadan used to be a reference clinic, University of Ibadan Teaching Hospital. People were coming from outside. Today, nobody comes. People were coming to Teaching Hospital here in Enugu, today nobody comes.” The NDC candidate further alleged that the capital budget of the National Assembly Clinic in 2024 exceeded the combined capital budgets of six federal teaching hospitals. “The budget of National Assembly Clinic, their budget for 2024, the capital budget of their clinic is more than—listen carefully—more than University of Ibadan Teaching Hospital capital budget, University of Lagos, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, Ahmadu Bello University, University of Jos, and Portharcourt put together!” He urged journalists to verify the figures and use their platforms to demand accountability from public officials. “You can Google it! That is the problem we have, because nobody… all of us are busy. Imagine if you put it in those teaching hospitals.” Obi also questioned the funding of the Aso Rock Clinic compared with the National Hospital, alleging that the presidential facility received substantially more funding. “Consistently, not for this present, the budget of Aso Rock Clinic is almost 10 times the budget of National Hospital. You can’t do that.” He cited the treatment of former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson during the COVID-19 pandemic as an example of a political leader relying on a public hospital. “When Boris Johnson was sick, they carried him to St Thomas’ when he had COVID. There was no clinic in Downing Street.” Obi urged editors to use their platforms to expose wasteful spending and hold political leaders accountable, warning that the consequences of poor governance would ultimately affect future generations. “We must… you people must help us. It’s your country. Help us to stop the abuse, or it will take its revenge on your children,” he said. The post Obi to editors: Hold politicians accountable, insist on issue-based campaigns appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Aladwa slams Uhuru over claim Raila was rigged in 2022
What Does the Climate Movement Do Now?
items.description: The day the Biden administration celebrated the first major piece of climate legislation in U.S. history, the weather happened to be sublime. The White House’s South Lawn, a billiard-table green, stretched out beneath a cerulean sky. Ben Beachy, who served as a special assistant to President Biden and would help oversee the law’s implementation, told me that “it felt like the dawn of a new era.” The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 was set to deliver hundreds of billions of dollars in federal investments to clean-energy programs, and to those partying in Washington, the law was a major step toward a long-sought goal: a plan for America’s future that addressed the realities of climate change. Four years on, the Republican Congress has mostly dismantled the IRA, electric-vehicle sales are in a slump, and the Trump administration is accelerating oil and gas development while axing environmental protections. The U.S. climate movement, Beachy said, “is currently experiencing a bout of dysphoria.” That’s putting it lightly. Longtime allies in the Democratic Party seem to be losing interest. Corporate America has all but ghosted climate advocates after making big pledges to go greener. Philanthropic support has gone squishy. Meanwhile, the planet is on track to speed past a 1.5-degree-Celsius increase in average global temperatures, the threshold that has been considered the bright line of danger since the Paris Agreement. Climate leaders have sought to project a keep-calm-and-carry-on attitude. “I would characterize this moment in time as just a moment in time,” Michael Brune, the former head of the Sierra Club and the CEO of the Clean Break Fund , told me. This is just an ebb tide, advocates insist, not all that different from past periods when climate slipped to the margins of the political conversation. There’s no doubt, however, that the dysphoria is real. I spoke with more than a dozen climate leaders spanning the academic, advocacy, and philanthropic sectors who told me, in different ways, that the American climate movement is unsure where to go from here. Having sunk to such lows so soon after climbing to such great heights, climate activists are scrambling to find the movement’s next big idea—some path that will lead them back out of the political wilderness. But right now they’re lost. If the Inflation Reduction Act managed to be one of most tepidly—and confusingly— titled laws in American history, it also represented a genuine breakthrough for climate action, an opportunity to begin reorganizing the U.S. economy around climate goals. Previously, the climate movement had two strategic strands, broadly speaking. The first focused on policy: pushing for international agreements (such as the Kyoto Protocol, which was never ratified) and national laws that would limit greenhouse-gas emissions (such as the Obama-era cap-and-trade bill that died in the Senate). Advocates scored their clearest win in 2015 with the signing of the Paris Agreement—though the signatories have failed to meet the accord’s lofty goals. The second strategy was to attack fossil fuels directly, along with the financial institutions underwriting them. The movement had some victories: The Keystone XL pipeline died; hundreds of U.S. colleges and churches divested from fossil-fuel companies; coal plants across the country were scheduled for closure. Then came the Green New Deal and its vision of an American manufacturing renaissance. After the neoliberal consensus that markets could manage carbon emissions fell apart, advocates and their allies in the Democratic Party got behind the idea that the best way to ratchet down emissions would be to build things: solar farms, electric-vehicle factories, high-speed rail. It was technocratic, sure, but also bold, a callback to the FDR era. Under industrial policy, the invisible hand of the market would be enclosed in a tight glove of federal priority-setting. The now-deflated Inflation Reduction Act was the wonky and somewhat less bold version of this ambition. Today, the overriding theory of change remains the same as ever: Back fossil fuels into the grave and drive a transition to renewable energy marked by speed and scale. But within the movement, there’s little consensus on how to do that. The climate movement does not lack for clever proposals—state-level cap-and-invest programs, grid modernization, make-polluters-pay laws, greater investments in climate-change adaptation. What it lacks is support that’s as resolute as it is broad. This has always been the climate movement’s Achilles’ heel, even at the high-water mark of the Greta Thunberg–inspired school strikes and mass marches in the years leading up to the pandemic. Climate change doesn’t score well on what public-opinion pollsters call “salience.” A majority of Americans are worried about climate change; in fact, the number of people who say they are concerned is near an all-time high . But when asked to rank climate change among other issues such as the cost of living, immigration, and health care, it turns out that most Americans aren’t very worried. This is a structural hurdle. For decades, climate advocates have anchored their efforts in grand ideals of generational responsibility, international solidarity, and care for other species. Although inspiring, those ideals might also sound— how to put this? —abstract. So, desperate for a way to connect with Americans and their immediate concerns, climate-movement leaders are searching for some political wave to surf. The most talked-about notion for a climate-action banner is the same issue everyone seems to be talking about: affordability. In this, the climate movement has a new ally—economics. As recently as a decade ago, “wind and solar were not cheaper. Period. Full stop,” Pete Maysmith, the president of the League of Conservation Voters, told me. “There were a bunch of reasons to do it, but it wasn’t affordability.” Now solar-plus-battery storage has become the cheapest form of new energy generation, as well as the quickest to build. Despite President Trump’s attacks on wind power, more than 90 percent of new electricity capacity that came online in the U.S. in 2025 was from renewables. That technological and market reality means that advocates can argue, for really the first time, that a clean-energy transition is good, not just for the planet, but also for pocketbooks. This is especially true as Trump’s war against Iran spikes household energy costs. The hope among advocates is that solar, batteries, and wind can go from being coded as liberal to being coded simply as cheap—the Costco of energy as opposed to the Whole Foods of energy, as Bill McKibben likes to say. This emphasis on cheap, clean energy is mostly a messaging strategy, but it does have real potential as policy. Environmental groups have used the clean-as-cheap argument to push public utilities commissions to approve renewable-energy projects , and Democrats in Congress have floated legislation, such as the Energy Bills Relief Act , that seeks to use the affordability argument to revive portions of the doomed IRA. But some climate advocates caution, usually off the record, that crowing about how cheap clean energy is risks overpromising. Even a full utility-sector embrace of renewables is unlikely to cut most Americans’ monthly bills in the short run, and will merely slow the projected increase in costs. “Cost plateau” is a tough political sell, and recent polling suggests that the clean-as-cheap message isn’t breaking through. So many climate advocates are looking to hitch the clean-energy future to populist concerns about AI, which is driving U.S. energy-demand growth and, in case you missed it, is strikingly unpopular. Some climate leaders think the AI boom could be a way to underwrite the transition to renewables. “We’re going to make the hyperscalers pay for it, and that’s what I think is going to likely catch on with Democratic presidential candidates,” John Podesta, a consigliere to the last three Democratic presidents and a longtime climate-action champion, told me. BeYONCE is the cringeworthy acronym for this idea—bring your own clean energy. A parallel notion is to force the AI giants to offset their electricity guzzling by paying for household energy upgrades—putting heat pumps in every home in exchange for being allowed to build data centers But that would ultimately ally the climate movement to one of the least popular industries in America. A community that is organizing to stop an AI data center because of its impact on local landscapes or the area’s rural character is unlikely to change positions because the AI facility comes with a giant solar farm. And for more radical climate activists, the notion of getting cozy with the AI bros raises major red flags. Aru Shiney-Ajay, the executive director of the Sunrise Movement, the youth-led climate group that helped popularize the Green New Deal, floated the idea that challenging AI build-out could be a political bank shot. She’s less interested in using the AI boom to also build renewable energy—à la Podesta—than she is in exploring whether antipathy to the tech giants can be married to antipathy to oil giants. “It’s basically a question of whether or not corporations get to control the land and the air and water around us, or whether ordinary people get to,” she told me. Leah Stokes, a professor of political science at UC Santa Barbara and the author of the new book The Carbon Wave , also proposed a political bank shot—connecting high energy costs and the data-center blowback to anger with Trump-administration corruption. Frustration with elites and “throw the bums out” populism could, in theory, lead some people to focus on the profiteering, and the massive political influence, of oil and gas companies. “People don’t like fossil-fuel companies,” Stokes told me. “It’s quite intuitive for a normal person to understand that those people are profiting and making billions while the rest of America can’t even pay their energy bills.” The climate leaders I talked with believe that Americans are thinking about climate change differently these days. They have a clearer understanding that it is contributing to painful increases in grocery costs and beginning to directly weigh on some families’ most valuable asset—their home; as homeowners in disaster-prone areas of California, Florida, and Louisiana are finding it more difficult to get insurance. It is time, some climate advocates believe, for a wholesale pivot from a morally centered movement to one centered on people’s material conditions—to reframe climate change as a kitchen-table issue for the first time. “You’ve never had more people who are experiencing climate change as a reality, not as a future problem,” Abigail Dillen, the president of Earthjustice, an environmental-law nonprofit, told me. “Real people at actual kitchen tables are talking about extreme heat, extreme weather, the insurance crisis.” Real talk among real people is, no doubt, essential for any political movement. It’s also insufficient. If a climate message begins with energy affordability or the simmering insurance crisis or the health impacts of wildfire smoke, it then needs to build to the ultimate goal of limiting carbon pollution, whether through the supply-side strategy of stopping future oil and gas projects or through the demand-side tactic of installing more solar panels that are hooked up to EVs. Perhaps that’s a bridge too far? The climate movement’s best ideas these days are little more than communication plays. The movement has a pile of white papers big enough to practically fuel a power plant’s boiler. But nearly 40 years after the NASA scientist James Hansen warned Congress of the dangers of global warming, a brutal mismatch exists between the number of Americans for whom climate change is priority No. 1 and the scale of the task at hand. All political movements go through times of boom and bust, and even the bust moments can be a fertile time for experimentation and visioning. On that point, Beachy, the former Biden-administration official, likes to quote (with no small amount of ironic self-knowing) the advice of the arch free-market fundamentalist Milton Friedman, to keep developing alternatives to favorite policies, “until the politically impossible becomes the politically inevitable.” Inevitable, though, can take an awfully long while to arrive, and addressing climate change is, infamously, a timed test. Despite its many bright ideas, the one thing the climate movement doesn’t have is time.

items.title: MSF annonce son retrait progressif d’Ansongo
items.description: Apres 14 ans de presence a Ansongo, Medecins Sans Frontieres prepare son retrait progressif de la zone. L'ONG a presente son plan de retrait, hier jeudi 24 septembre, aux autorites administratives et communautaires. Elle a egalement dresse le bilan de ses activites. En 2025, MSF a consacre plus d'un milliard 36 millions de francs CFA a l'appui au district sanitaire, notamment pour la prise en charge des urgences. Cette annee, cet appui s'eleve a plus d'un milliard 107 millions de francs CFA. Les activites de l'ONG doivent prendre fin en 2027. items.title: ‘Don’t betray me’ — Mourinho warns Real Madrid players
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye José Mourinho has warned his Real Madrid players that trust is non-negotiable, as he emphasised the importance of trust between players and coach in his bid to build a new winning team for the Spanish side. Mourinho, who returned to the Santiago Bernabéu this summer 13 years after his first spell in charge, made the remarks while discussing his managerial philosophy and stating the “non-negotiable” rules for his squad to follow. “When I say don’t betray me, of course, I’m speaking about football. Don’t betray me, and I’ll always be there for you,” Mourinho told the Bet It Drives Show, as reported by ESPN. The veteran manager, known for his strict approach, also outlined the rules he expects his players to follow, insisting that even the club’s biggest stars must be disciplined. “There are rules that are not negotiable,” Mourinho said. “If you report at 9 a.m., it’s 9 a.m. for everybody. If you arrive at 9.15, even if you’re a superstar, you just can’t. I don’t accept it … But another thing is giving them freedom to express themselves.” Mourinho said being a professional footballer extends beyond what happens on the pitch, stressing that players must make sacrifices if they want to reach the highest level. “You are a football player 24 hours a day,” he said. “Everything reflects the job. What you eat, what you drink, how you sleep, even things in your private life. You cannot ski. You cannot ride a bike.” “You fall off your bike, and you don’t play three matches maybe, or maybe worse, maybe you break a leg … There are a lot of things that you have to give up to be a football player. “If you feel it’s a hobby, you’re dead. There’s always a relationship between what you achieve and what you give up.” Mourinho also revealed that Real Madrid approached him to return after a difficult period for the club, with the Spanish giants seeking to rebuild following two seasons without a major trophy. “After two seasons where the biggest club in the world didn’t have the best results and a little ‘divorce’ with the fans, the club contacted me,” he said. “They told me, ‘We know you. You know us. You know the club, you know the culture. “We need you. We need you to rebuild. We need you to start again an amazing decade that the club had. We need a person with your profile.’” The Portuguese coach has endured a difficult start to his second spell at Madrid, with the club six points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona and having suffered a derby defeat by rivals Atletico. The post ‘Don’t betray me’ — Mourinho warns Real Madrid players appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Keïtayah : un présumé malfaiteur interpellé en flagrant délit lors du vandalisme d’une boutique
items.description: Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le grand banditisme, le Secrétariat général à la Présidence, chargé de la lutte contre le crime organisé, a procédé à l’interpellation d’un présumé malfaiteur, surpris en flagrant délit de vandalisme dans une boutique située à Keïtayah, dans la nuit. Le nommé Amara Bangoura, ferrailleur de profession, présenté ce vendredi 25 septembre 2026 à Kaloum, a reconnu les faits qui lui sont reprochés, notamment un vol aggravé commis de nuit et en bande, avec escalade, effraction et pénétration dans une boutique après déchirure des tôles. Des faits prévus et punis par les dispositions de l’article 374 et suivants du Code pénal. S’exprimant sur instruction du Secrétaire général et avec l’approbation du procureur, le commissaire principal de police Foromo Soropogui est revenu sur le mode opératoire des présumés malfaiteurs : « Les Services Spéciaux vous présente ce matin un bandit, d'apparence trompeuse et d'une dangerosité mystique opérant en groupe de trois éléments. Dans la nuit du 02 septembre 2026 aux environs de 4 heures du matin, les nommés Amara BANGOURA alias « Makalos », un second surnommé « Gniné » et le troisième « Papis » sont parti à Keïtayah dans le domicile d'un Citoyen, au moment pluvieux, escalader le mur, puis pénétrer dans la boutique par effraction: c’est-à-dire usage de ciseau et marteau pour déchirer la tôle et le plafond. Ouvrir la porte, transporter et stocker dans les herbes à 60 mètres de la scène de crime, des marchandises diverses et numéraires». Le commissaire principal de la Direction centrale de la lutte contre le crime organisé a poursuivi : «Faits constatés par les habitants voisins très solidaires, et avec l'intervention rapide d'une équipe des services spéciaux, l'un des malfrats fût arrêté et mis à notre disposition. Les marchandises volées furent récupérées, sauf le montant de 3.750.000 francs guinéens emportés par « Gninè » et « Papis » en fuite. À en croire ce responsable des Services spéciaux, les deux autres mis en cause seraient des habitués des juridictions : «Gninè » et «Papis » sont des récidivistes déférés au tribunal de Dubréka en début de cette année», a-t-il rappelé. Devant les caméras et les micros, le présumé délinquant Amara Bangoura, interpellé par les agents des Services spéciaux, a reconnu les faits qui lui sont reprochés, en ces termes : « Je reconnu les faits. On était trois mais moi je connais pas là-bas, moi, c’est mon grand qui est venu me dire de l'accompagner, je ne savais pas qu’on partait ici. On est venu jusqu'à cet endroit comme il ne voulais que je sache ce qu’il veux faire, il m'a dit de m'arrêter au carrefour là-bas je me suis arrêté au Carrefour et eux ils sont descendu en bas. Quelques temps après j’ai vu grand Papis transporter des colis et les amener vers moi et m’ont dit maintenant on va les transporter à la maison, je lui ait dit non, je ne peux pas le faire car je suis malade je ne vais pas transporter les colis», a-t-il déclaré, tout en soulignant qu’il s’agissait, selon lui, de sa première participation à ce type d’opération. Mamadou Yaya Barry L’article Keïtayah : un présumé malfaiteur interpellé en flagrant délit lors du vandalisme d’une boutique est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: AFCON 2027: 21 spots up for grabs, 3 countries already qualified — all you need to know
items.description: The race for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON, has officially begun, with 48 countries battling for 21 available places at the tournament in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. The three East African countries will host the AFCON 2027 edition and have already secured automatic qualification, leaving the remaining nations to fight for the 21 spots still available. The qualification format also means that not every group will produce two qualifiers, making the race particularly significant for teams drawn alongside the three hosts. Here is everything to know about the AFCON 2027 qualifying process. 1. 48 countries are competing for 21 places A total of 48 nations have been drawn into 12 groups of four teams. Each team will play six matches — home and away against the other three countries in its group. At the end of the qualifying campaign, 21 teams will join the three hosts to complete the 24-team AFCON 2027 lineup. 2. Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda are already qualified As the three host nations, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda have automatic places at AFCON 2027. Their participation does not depend on their performance in the qualifying groups. However, they will still compete in the qualifying campaign, creating a special situation in the three groups containing the hosts. 3. How many teams qualify from each group? In the nine groups without a host nation, two teams will qualify. That means: Group A — 2 qualifiers Group B — 2 qualifiers Group C — 2 qualifiers Group E — 2 qualifiers Group F — 2 qualifiers Group G — 2 qualifiers Group I — 2 qualifiers Group J — 2 qualifiers Group K — 2 qualifiers That produces 18 qualifiers. The remaining three places will come from the groups containing the host nations. 4. Only one non-host team can qualify from the three host groups This is where the qualification race becomes different. The three host nations are spread across three groups: Group D South Africa Guinea Kenya Eritrea Group H Tunisia Uganda Libya Botswana Group L Nigeria Madagascar Tanzania Guinea-Bissau Because Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania are already qualified as hosts, only one additional team can qualify from each of those groups. Therefore: Group D produces one additional qualifier Group H produces one additional qualifier Group L produces one additional qualifier That gives the remaining three places needed to reach 21 qualifiers. 5. Nigeria’s Group L is particularly important Nigeria have been drawn in Group L alongside Madagascar, Tanzania and Guinea-Bissau. Tanzania are already qualified as one of the hosts. As a result, Nigeria do not need to finish in a conventional top-two position to qualify. Instead, the Super Eagles must finish above Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau to take the group’s single available qualification place. This makes every point in Nigeria’s six matches potentially crucial. 6. Who cannot qualify from the host groups? The three hosts cannot be eliminated from AFCON 2027 because they already have guaranteed places. However, the other teams in their groups are effectively competing for one qualification ticket. For example, in Group L, Nigeria, Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau are competing for the one available place alongside already-qualified Tanzania. The same principle applies to South Africa, Guinea and Eritrea in Group D, and Tunisia, Libya and Botswana in Group H. 7. What happens in the other nine groups? The qualification process is more straightforward in the other groups. The top two teams after the six group matches will qualify for AFCON 2027. There is therefore little room for error, with teams needing to accumulate enough points to finish inside the top two. 8. Full list of the 12 qualifying groups Group A Morocco, Gabon, Niger, Lesotho Group B Egypt, Angola, Malawi, South Sudan Group C Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, The Gambia, Somalia Group D South Africa, Guinea, Kenya, Eritrea Group E DR Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Sierra Leone, Zimbabwe Group F Burkina Faso, Benin, Mauritania, Central African Republic Group G Cameroon, Comoros, Namibia, Congo Group H Tunisia, Uganda, Libya, Botswana Group I Algeria, Zambia, Togo, Burundi Group J Senegal, Mozambique, Sudan, Ethiopia Group K Mali, Cape Verde, Rwanda, Liberia Group L Nigeria, Madagascar, Tanzania, Guinea-Bissau 9. When will the qualifiers be played? The qualifying campaign is scheduled across three international windows. The first two matchdays are being played in September and October 2026, followed by further fixtures in November 2026 and the final two matchdays in March 2027. By the end of Matchday 6, all 21 remaining AFCON places will have been decided. 10. When is AFCON 2027? The 2027 Africa Cup of Nations will be staged in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19 June to 17 July, 2027. The tournament will feature 24 teams, consisting of the three automatic qualifiers and the 21 countries that emerge from the qualifying campaign. The competition will bring together the continent’s leading national teams for the first AFCON edition to be jointly hosted by the three East African countries. items.title: Classement FIFA : le Maroc retrouve la 5e place mondiale
items.description: Les Lions de l’Atlas occupent désormais la 5e place du classement FIFA avec 1.803,99 points. Le Maroc profite du match nul du Brésil face à l’Australie (1-1) en amical pour dépasser la Seleçao et égaler son meilleur classement historique. Le Maroc grimpe à nouveau dans la hiérarchie mondiale. Les Lions de l’Atlas occupent ce vendredi 25 septembre la cinquième place du classement FIFA, mis à jour en temps réel. Avec 1.803,99 points, la sélection nationale devance désormais le Brésil, qui recule au sixième rang après son match nul (1-1) contre l’Australie lors d’une rencontre amicale. Cette progression permet aux Lions de l’Atlas d’égaler le meilleur classement jamais atteint par une sélection africaine. Le Maroc avait déjà occupé la cinquième position mondiale le 20 juin dernier, après sa victoire contre l’Écosse (1-0) lors de la phase de groupes de la Coupe du monde 2026. Le top 5 mondial reste par ailleurs inchangé dans sa composition, avec toutefois le Maroc qui prend désormais la place du Brésil. L’Espagne conserve la première position après son sacre mondial, devant l’Argentine, la France et l’Angleterre. items.title: Téléphone aux toilettes : quand le petit écran fait durer la pause
items.description: Aux toilettes aussi, le smartphone semble avoir trouve sa place. a Bamako, certains ne s'y rendent plus sans leur telephone, histoire de repondre a un message, scroller sur les reseaux sociaux ou simplement passer le temps. Une habitude parfois amusante pour ceux qui la pratiquent, mais beaucoup moins pour ceux qui attendent derriere la porte. Et selon des medecins, prolonger son sejour aux toilettes n'est pas non plus sans consequences pour la sante. Dans certaines familles et meme sur certains lieux de travail, voir une personne entrer aux toilettes avec son telephone n'a plus rien d'exceptionnel. Pour certains, cette pratique est devenue une veritable habitude. « Je me sens a l'aise dans les toilettes avec mon telephone. C'est devenu comme une addiction, je ne peux pas m'en empecher » , temoigne Samba Diallo. Fatimata Maïga, elle, en parle avec le sourire : « ca a un goût inexplicable. » Elle reconnaît toutefois qu'il vaut mieux eviter d'en faire une habitude. Pour d'autres, le reflexe remonte a l'enfance. Un interlocuteur qui prefere rester anonyme, que nous appellerons Moussa, raconte avoir ete inspire par son grand-pere. « Lorsqu'on etait petit, il rentrait tres souvent avec sa radio pour ecouter les informations. J'ai pris ca comme une bonne chose et j'ai commence cette habitude vers mes 15 ou 16 ans » , explique-t-il. Aujourd'hui, Moussa utilise son telephone pour signaler sa presence aux toilettes. « Je mettais mon telephone en musique et je rentrais avec pour signaler ma presence et aussi pour imiter mon grand-pere. J'y ai pris goût et jusqu'a present, je continue de le faire » , raconte-t-il. Pour lui, cette habitude ne pose pas vraiment de probleme : « En tout cas, ca ne me gene pas. » Un reflexe lie a notre rapport permanent au numerique Pour Sekou Doumbia, ingenieur en securite reseau a l'Agence des technologies de l'information et de la communication (AGTIC), cette pratique s'explique notamment par notre rapport de plus en plus constant au numerique. « L'utilisation du telephone aux toilettes s'explique principalement par notre incapacite moderne a tolerer l'ennui et le vide » , estime-t-il. Le smartphone permet ainsi de combler les quelques minutes passees aux toilettes. Une maniere de rester connecte, meme dans un moment qui etait autrefois davantage consacre a une simple pause. Une habitude qui agace ceux qui attendent Si certains apprecient ces minutes supplementaires avec leur telephone, ceux qui patientent a l'exterieur ont parfois un tout autre avis. « Ceux qui rentrent avec leur telephone dans les toilettes le font par conviction. Personnellement, je ne vois pas l'utilite. Et puis, ce n'est meme pas bien de parler dans les toilettes » , estime un homme d'environ une trentaine d'annees rencontre dans les rues de Bamako. Il dit preferer faire vite : « Je n'ai meme pas ce temps. Je fais mon besoin et je sors aussitot. » Meme son de cloche chez cet autre jeune rencontre sur place : « Tu ne peux pas prendre ton temps a manipuler ton telephone dans les toilettes alors qu'il y a des gens qui attendent dehors. Pour moi, ce n'est pas serieux. » Rester longtemps aux toilettes, quels risques pour la sante ? Au-dela de la gene occasionnee, rester longtemps assis aux toilettes peut egalement avoir des consequences sur la sante, selon le Dr Salaha Garba. « Rester assis longtemps dans les toilettes augmente la pression sur les veines de l'anus, ce qui peut favoriser les maladies hemorroïdaires » , explique-t-il. Selon le medecin, une position prolongee peut egalement favoriser une sensation de jambes lourdes. Le praticien recommande donc de ne pas prolonger inutilement le sejour aux toilettes. Selon lui, cinq a six minutes peuvent suffire dans la plupart des cas. Meme en cas de diarrhee, il conseille de sortir apres quelques minutes, de marcher un peu et de boire suffisamment d'eau avant de retourner aux toilettes si necessaire. Le smartphone peut donc accompagner cette pause, mais a condition de ne pas la transformer en longue seance de navigation. Quelques minutes peuvent rapidement devenir beaucoup plus longues lorsque le petit ecran capte toute l'attention. L’article Téléphone aux toilettes : quand le petit écran fait durer la pause est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Retour de New York : Mamadi Doumbouya accueilli par une forte mobilisation à Conakry
items.description: Après avoir pris part aux travaux de la 81ᵉ session ordinaire de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies à New York, le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, a regagné Conakry ce vendredi 25 septembre 2026. Son avion a atterri dans la matinée à l’aéroport international Ahmed-Sékou-Touré, au terme de plusieurs jours consacrés à une importante séquence diplomatique aux États-Unis. À son arrivée, le chef de l’État a été accueilli dans le cadre d’un cérémonial officiel auquel ont pris part plusieurs hautes personnalités de la République. Le Premier ministre, chef du gouvernement, les présidents des institutions républicaines, les membres du gouvernement, ainsi que des responsables civils et militaires figuraient parmi les personnalités présentes à l’aéroport. La cérémonie a également enregistré la présence de représentants des missions diplomatiques et consulaires accréditées en Guinée, ainsi que de responsables d’organisations internationales. Cette mobilisation avait été annoncée par le Cabinet civil de la Présidence, qui avait convié les autorités et personnalités concernées à prendre part au cérémonial d’accueil. Au-delà du dispositif officiel, une foule nombreuse s’est mobilisée aux abords de l’aéroport et le long de l’itinéraire présidentiel, brandissant notamment les couleurs nationales. Une importante présence citoyenne aux côtés des forces de sécurité chargées d’encadrer le dispositif. Ce retour intervient après la participation de Mamadi Doumbouya aux travaux de la 81ᵉ Assemblée générale de l’ONU, au cours desquels il a porté les positions et priorités de la Guinée sur la scène internationale. À New York, le chef de l’État a également eu des échanges avec plusieurs partenaires et a rencontré le secrétaire général des Nations unies, António Guterres. La séquence new-yorkaise désormais achevée, le président de la République retrouve ainsi Conakry, où son retour a été marqué par un important cérémonial républicain et une forte mobilisation populaire.

items.title: Discours contraires aux bonnes mœurs contre Victorine Ndèye : le procés de Désiré Pascal Maty renvoyé au 02 octobre
items.description: L’ancienne ministre de la Microfinance et de l’Économie sociale et solidaire, Victorine Anquediche Ndéye, s ’est désistée de sa constitution de partie civile et n’était pas devant la barre du tribunal des flagrants délits de Dakar ce vendredi, mais l’action publique se poursuit contre Désiré Pascal Maty. Ce dernier, âgé de 34 ans et agent dans le ministère qui a été dirigé par Mme Ndéye, est poursuivi pour des faits présumés de discours contraires aux bonnes mœurs, d’injures publiques, de menaces et de diffamation. L’affaire qui venait à la barre pour la première fois a été renvoyée au 2 octobre après que le tribunal a suivi le représentant du parquet qui s’est opposé à la demande de liberté provisoire formulée par la défense. Le représentant de la société a fait remarquer que n’importe qui aurait pu déposer une plainte vu la nature des propos tenus par le prévenu, dans les réseaux sociaux. A lire aussi : Offense au chef de l’Etat – discours contraires aux bonnes mœurs : peines fermes et amende pour Lamignou Darou et ses co-prévenus Interpellé par la Division spéciale de cybersécurité (Dsc), Désiré Pascal Maty, qui a été placé sous mandat de dépôt le 23 septembre, a fait une publication jugée discourtoise envers le maire de Niaguis. Cette dernière a déposé une plainte après avoir été alertée sur la sortie de Désiré Pascal Maty, par des proches. Au cours de l’enquête, le prévenu avait soutenu avoir réagi suite à des propos de Mme Ndéye. Hadja Diaw GAYE
